correctness.rationale: The domination condition for K_{k,k} is equivalent to the equivariant union (∂Δ_L*∂Δ_R)∪Δ_L∪Δ_R, where both whole-shore simplices are attached by full boundaries. The A_k action is orientation-preserving on the standard Coxeter reflection sphere; the A_k quotient is a sphere S^{k−2}, while the S_k quotient is one closed chamber ball. Taking A_k×A_k makes join S^{2k−3}; both null attaching spheres yield two S^{k−1} summands. Exchanging shores diagonalizes the factor-swap into V+ and sign-reversed V−, yielding S^{k−2}*RP^{k−2}≃Σ^{k−1}RP^{k−2}. The two shore balls become one ball attached along a nullhomotopic S^{k−2}, giving an extra S^{k−1}. The full wreath S_k×S_k quotient uses contractible chamber balls and is contractible. Integral RP homology yields Z/2 in degree k for k>=4, and k=4 gives S³∨M(Z/2,4). Checked source finite k=3,4 Burnside/Lefschetz checker and independently verified the suspension degrees, connectivity and Euler predictions; finite Euler alone would not prove the homotopy claim.
